$comment: The journey engine's vocabulary and its weights, kept out of code so the reasoning can be read by somebody who does not read JavaScript. Two rules govern everything in this file. First: a signal is only scored if the dataset actually holds it. A country's `calls`, its `months`, its operator, its region and how many of its twenty-six write-ups fall under a chosen lens are all real; how a traveller likes to travel and who they are travelling with are not recorded anywhere, so they are collected, carried to the operator, and never scored. Second: a `days` band is a planning convention, not a claim about the country — it decides how many stages a journey is shaped into, and the page says so.

weights.$comment: Out of 100. Change a number here and the ranking changes; nothing in the engine hard-codes a preference.
weights.$operator: Zero, deliberately. It was 10, and it was defended as 'not a quality claim — a claim about who answers the telephone'. That was true when three local operators were the only product: in those three countries somebody of ours picked up, and everywhere else somebody else did. It is not true now. The ground journey is Afrinkong's own in all fifty-four, so who answers the telephone is the same answer everywhere, and ten points for owning the company as well is a thumb on the scale that serves us rather than the person who asked about wildlife. Whether we own the operator is still shown as a reason on the recommendation — it is worth knowing — it just no longer decides which country a traveller is sent to.

pacing.label: A long weekend
pacing.line: One place, properly, instead of three badly.

pacing.label: Four to seven days
pacing.line: Two places close enough that the road between them is not the trip.

pacing.label: Eight to fourteen days
pacing.line: A country properly, or two that share a border.

pacing.label: Two weeks and more
pacing.line: Long enough to stop counting, and to go where the road is slow.

pacing.label: I'm flexible
pacing.line: We will shape it round what you actually want to see.

carried: Neither how you like to travel nor who you are travelling with is recorded against any country in this dataset, so neither one moves a country up or down the list. Both are carried into the enquiry, where a person who lives there reads them.
